result.topic_en: For an elastic rod bent into a closed ring, Euler uses the periodicity condition at the point A (s = 0, a, 2a, ...) to show that α = β = δ = 0 and sin ω = 0, giving simple tones proportional to i², i.e. in the ratio 1, 4, 9, 16, ....

$0 = \alpha + \beta + \delta$. Iam ſtatuamus $s = a$, et quia iterum
in idem punctum A incidimus ponendo breuitatis gra-
tia $\frac{a}{f} = \omega$, fieri oportet
$$0 = \alpha e^{\omega} + \beta e^{-\omega} + \gamma \sin.\omega + \delta \cos.\omega,$$
atque idem euenire debet, ſi ponamus $s = 2a$, ſiue $3a$,
ſiue $4a$ etc., vnde naſcentur ſequentes aequationes:
$$0 = \alpha e^{2\omega} + \beta e^{-2\omega} + \gamma \sin.2\omega + \delta \cos.2\omega,$$
$$0 = \alpha e^{3\omega} + \beta e^{-3\omega} + \gamma \sin.3\omega + \delta \cos.3\omega,$$
etc. etc.
quibus omnibus ſimul ſatisfieri nequit, niſi ſit $\alpha = 0$,
$\beta = 0$ et $\delta = 0$; tum vero neceſſe eſt, vt ſimul fiat
$$\sin.\omega = 0,\ \sin.2\omega = 0,\ \sin.3\omega = 0 \text{ etc.}$$
quod in genere eueniet, ſumendo $\omega = i\pi$, denotante $i$ nu-
